source_snapshot.gpt_v2: BLOCKED correctly requires a dedicated account, protected injection, non-disclosing verification and rollback, but treats the User ID, operation and 16/20-byte encoding as vendor-defined.

old_problem: The historical review correctly protected credentials but incorrectly required a vendor password schema. IPMI App 47h standardizes a six-bit User ID, 16/20-byte selector, set/test/enable/disable operations, fixed payload lengths and password-test completion codes. The remaining password policy, dedicated identity, vault mechanism and original-secret rollback are Project execution inputs. Keeping the row blocked also obscured that enable/disable are separate operation values and need not be touched to test password replacement.
disposition_reason: Use one enabled disposable non-production User ID with no active session, a protected original credential and known 16- or 20-byte storage size. Generate one non-null temporary credential of the same approved size in a vault, send exactly one App 47h set-password operation, verify it once using the standard test-password operation and once through a fresh least-privilege login, then set the protected original credential exactly once, test it once and verify the restored login. Name, enable state, access, privilege and other users remain unchanged. Secrets never enter arguments, files, output or evidence; enable/disable operations, null/default/shared values, negative-password probes, automatic retry and log clearing are prohibited.
decision_basis: Master XLSX rows 1027-1029, exact same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT second review, tests_gpt_merged, selection manifest and historical V3.1 record were directly read. The exact code is unique. Formal queue sequence 64 was independently verified and its source XLSX row directly read as Functionality row 1055 / Wistron-BMC-00345-V003 / variant 301579e363a9a03b.

IPMI v2.0 section 22.30 defines App NetFn 06h command 47h. Request byte 1 contains the 16/20-byte selector and nonzero six-bit User ID; byte 2 operation 10b sets and 11b tests a password, while 00b/01b disable/enable the user and are excluded from this row.

Password data is a fixed sixteen or twenty-byte octet string. The BMC must support twenty-byte passwords for configurable IPMI v2.0 users; a twenty-byte password cannot establish IPMI v1.5, while a sixteen-byte value can be zero-padded for RMCP+ compatibility. The Project protocol fixture therefore selects one size and the restore must use the original stored size.

The BMC accepts all octet values and does not enforce the console's human password policy. The secret generator and runner must apply the Project policy consistently and forbid an ASCII null-string or zero/default/shared credential even though the protocol can encode it.

The standard test-password operation is the non-disclosing verification oracle: 00h means match, 80h means correct size but mismatch and 81h means wrong size. No raw password is returned. This case performs only positive tests; deliberate wrong-password/size tests could affect lockout policy and are excluded.

A command completion/test match does not prove remote authentication. A fresh session using the temporary credential must complete one harmless Get Device ID and close, followed after restoration by the same bounded check with the original credential.

Username, enabled state, per-channel access and privilege belong to App 45h/47h enable-disable/43h and remain independent baselines. Password replacement is not credited for those adjacent source cases and must not alter them.

ED-02/ED-03/ED-13 allow exact standard BMC semantics without OEM guesses; ED-15 governs authoritative unsupported N/A; ED-18/ED-30 require protected least-privilege authorization; ED-19 preserves audit evidence; ED-28 requires isolation/recovery; ED-33 through ED-38 govern package readiness, confirmation, cleanup, non-retry and engineer verdict separation.

test_case.test_name: IPMI Set User Password (App 06h/47h) protected temporary credential and exact original restore
test_case.purpose: Replace the password of exactly one disposable least-privilege BMC test User ID through a protected channel, prove standard password-test and effective login with no disclosure, restore the original credential and prove authentication/access state fully recovered.
required_package: Approved BMC/firmware/channel with standard App 47h support, exact target User ID and protocol applicability (RMCP+ 20-byte or approved 16-byte compatibility path)
Enabled configurable dedicated non-production/non-root/non-recovery User ID with fixed approved name/access/privilege, no active session and an independent Administrator control/recovery identity

Vault-held original credential plus authoritative original size tag (16 or 20 bytes), already verified before the window without exposing it, and owner-approved single-use randomly generated non-null temporary credential of the same size

Secret-safe Set/Test Password runner using protected stdin/descriptor/secret provider rather than argv, environment dump, plaintext file or console output; exact package version/hash, memory zeroization and zero automatic retries

Immutable User Name/User Access/channel/all-user/session/audit baseline and a non-disclosing verifier that records only operation, target, size, completion, session correlation and secret-reference/version hashes
Immediate security approval, bad-password/lockout threshold awareness, vault rotation/revocation procedure and exact original-secret restore path
test_case.test_command: AUTHORIZED CREDENTIAL-ROTATION PROCEDURE; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Preserve security/audit logs and do not clear them. Through the independent Administrator path, verify the exact dedicated TEST_USER_ID, name/access/privilege/enable state, no active test-user session, protocol and ORIGINAL_SIZE in {16,20}; retrieve ORIGINAL_SECRET only through the approved vault and generate TEMP_SECRET of the same size/policy. Display only target, size and opaque secret-reference hashes for immediate approval. Send exactly once App 06h/47h with byte1 = TEST_USER_ID plus size bit, byte2 operation 02h (set password), and fixed-length TEMP_SECRET from protected memory; require completion 00h and zero the transmitted buffer. Send exactly once operation 03h (test password) for TEMP_SECRET with the same size; require 00h, never persist response-adjacent secret bytes, then establish one fresh least-privilege session using protected TEMP_SECRET, issue only Get Device ID and close. In a finally path send exactly once operation 02h with ORIGINAL_SECRET and ORIGINAL_SIZE, require 00h, then one operation 03h must return 00h and one original-credential Get Device ID session must succeed and close. Verify name/enable/access/privilege/other-user/session/audit baselines and revoke TEMP_SECRET reference. Never use operations 00h/01h, target User1/production/admin/recovery identities, change size during the run, use null/default/shared secrets, conduct mismatch tests, expose a credential, clear logs or automatically retry.
test_case.expected_result: The exact dedicated User ID receives one temporary secret of the approved original size. Set returns 00h, one positive Test Password returns 00h and a fresh least-privilege session with the temporary credential completes Get Device ID and closes. The exact original credential is then set once, its positive test and fresh login both succeed, and the temporary secret is revoked/zeroized. Username, enabled state, access, privilege, channel policy, other users, sessions and audit health remain unchanged; evidence contains no secret. 80h/81h, generic error, timeout, wrong target/size, login failure, lockout, exposure, unrelated drift or failed original restore is FAIL/NOT READY without retry; authoritative lack of any configurable disposable user permits N/A.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact Source Key/variant, approved disposable User ID, verified protected original secret/size, one same-size temporary set, 00h completion, one 00h positive password test, one bounded temporary login, one exact original set, one 00h original test/login, secret disposal and unchanged identity/access/other-user/audit baselines. A password-status guess, high-level success without Test Password and login, enable/disable operation, size change, null/default/shared/production credential, deliberate negative test, secret in argv/env dump/file/log/evidence, retry, unrelated session action, log clearing or incomplete restoration cannot pass. Missing vault/original secret/size/dedicated account/recovery is NOT READY rather than Pending review.
safety_gate: Target only an enabled disposable configurable User ID with no active session. Exclude User 1/null, fixed production, shared, root/admin and every recovery/control identity.

Original credential and exact size must be verified and recoverable before mutation. Temporary secret uses the same size and Project policy; never use a null string, default, reused or human-shared value.

Secrets enter only protected runner memory and are zeroized after each request. Prohibit command-line `-P`, plaintext temp files, shell history, process/environment dumps, debug packet payloads and any evidence containing secret bytes.
Use only operation 02h set and 03h positive test. Do not disable/enable the user or intentionally test an incorrect secret/size; preserve bad-password counters and lockout state.
Preserve audit/security logs and all identity/access baselines. Close only the two sessions created by this test and revoke the temporary secret reference after original restoration.

No automatic retry. A timeout is an ambiguous credential state: stop, keep the independent control session, and have the security owner execute the one approved original-secret restore rather than probing repeatedly.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/variant, BMC/firmware/channel/protocol, dedicated User ID ownership and no-active-session baseline
Security approval; runner/version/hash; opaque ORIGINAL/TEMP vault reference hashes and size/policy attestations without secret bytes
Redacted set-temporary metadata and 00h completion, positive Test Password 00h, temporary-credential Get Device ID/close correlation
Redacted set-original metadata and 00h completion, original positive test/login/close, TEMP reference revocation and memory-zeroization attestation
Unchanged identity/access/other-user/session/audit comparison, incident/recovery record if any and engineer PASS/FAIL/NOT READY/N/A verdict
test_case.recovery: The normal rollback is one Set User Password operation 02h for the exact TEST_USER_ID using ORIGINAL_SIZE and ORIGINAL_SECRET from the protected vault, followed by one positive operation-03h test and one original-credential least-privilege login. On an ambiguous temporary-set response, do not retry or probe wrong secrets; keep the independent Administrator session and perform the approved original restore once. If that response is ambiguous, the security owner may perform one bounded positive original-secret test under the known lockout policy, then use the documented console/service recovery path rather than repeated authentication. On exposure, revoke both affected secret versions as an incident, rotate through the independent path, preserve audit logs and verify no other user changed.

source_conflict.reason: Official section 22.30 supplies User ID, size, operation, payload and verification semantics. The parameterized protected-secret procedure retains actual password-change/login/restore coverage, separates enable/name/access commands and removes the conflicting log-clear boilerplate.

blocked.reason: Core Set/Test User Password semantics and non-disclosing validation are standardized. Dedicated User ID, vault secrets/size, policy, runner and independent recovery are finite security packages rather than missing engineering definitions.
